about: E1 (F4): each test-spec row names the weaker implementation its oracle rejects (`Stand-in rejected:` at the end of `red`, since a row holds exactly its six keys until the field is built), and the summary lists the entry points. Written against feat/shiploop-templates-6d625a (arm T, the text-only batch); a field T already states is not repeated.

edits.old:
suites says whether the target keeps state); a guard that only checks a file is not RED. "characterisation" if
   it already passes.
edits.new:
suites says whether the target keeps state); a guard that only checks a file is not RED. "characterisation" if
   it already passes. End each row's `red` with `Stand-in rejected: <the simplest wrong implementation of the
   entry point that this oracle fails>`; a row whose oracle a do-nothing or accept-anything version would also
   pass rejects nothing: strengthen its oracle.

edits.old: and one case per documented throw or refusal branch.
edits.new:
and one case per documented throw or refusal branch. In `summary` write `Entry points:` and, per public entry
   point the item adds or changes, the row IDs that call it and the stand-ins they reject.

edits.old: "red": "<how the case fails before the change>"
edits.new: "red": "<how the case fails before the change>; Stand-in rejected: <the simplest wrong implementation this oracle fails>"
